objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with skin lesions on the forehead.

fragments.text: The patient reports the recent appearance of several brown, greasy, seemingly superficial lesions on his forehead. He mentions they appeared a few weeks ago and has not noticed any recent changes in size or color. He attempted to scrape them off, assuming they were dirt or a smear, but they persisted. No itching or pain is associated with the lesions.
Hypertension, controlled with medication. No history of skin cancer or chronic skin diseases.
Retired school teacher. Non-smoker. Enjoys gardening and spends time outdoors.
Denies weight loss, fever, night sweats, or any recent illnesses.

exam_leaves.text: Multiple well-defined, round to oval, brown, greasy plaques ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 cm in diameter located predominantly on the forehead.
Lesions are slightly raised, with a waxy texture. No tenderness or warmth on palpation.
Not available but typically shows cerebriform pattern and milia-like cysts in seborrheic keratoses.

test_leaves.text: Not performed but would show proliferation of benign keratinocytes, horn cysts, and a papillomatous surface if done.
